To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) robust optimization of linear control in a discrete-time linear dynamical system becomes computationally tractible if, instead of the traditional parameterization of a control law, one uses the so-called “purified output” parameterization of the control law and (ii) robust optimization of a linear time-invariant control law in a linear system is computationally tractible as well, the control law being parameterized by the “purified outputs”.

, in a discrete time time-invariant linear dynamical system, robust optimization of finite-horizon linear control and infinite-horizon linear time-invariant control, affected by uncertainty, can be carried out in an efficient way via solving a finite set of convex programs, provided that the control is parameterized via a special re-parameterization, the so called “pure output” re-parameterization, which, in the case of finite horizon, is a bi-affine parameterization, and in the case

(1) the problem of robust optimization of linear control in discrete time linear dynamically uncertain system is computationally tractable, (2) the computational tractability of the problem is achieved by re-parameterization of control law, (3) the computational tractable re-parameterization is based on a new notion of “purified output”, (4) the new parameterization of control law is bi-affine, (5) optimization of bi-affine control law reduces to solving a convex optimization program
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a methodology for robust optimization of linear time-invariant control systems in the presence of uncertainty.
the problem of robust optimization of control of discrete time linear dynamics systems affected by uncertain disturbances.
the development of computationally tractable methodologies of robust synthesis of linear output-based control laws for linear discrete time systems with uncertain inputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach provides a new way of looking at robust control, in which the control is not a function of the state and the disturbance, but rather a function of a new set of variables, which we call “purified outputs” or “innovations.”

, with our new methodology, the synthesis of robust control laws for linear discrete time uncertain systems, which are computationally intractable with traditional methods, becomes computationally tractible.

the proposed methodology, which is based on the use of the so called purified output, is a powerful tool for the design of robust control laws for discrete time linear systems affected by uncertainty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the control of uncertain linear discrete time systems is computationally tractable, if one passes from the traditional parameterization of the control law to a specific reparameterization, representing the law as affine control law.
the proposed methodology allows to solve a variety of robust optimization problems for discrete time linear systems affected by uncertain disturbances, in a computationally tractable way.
we are able to solve the problem of robust control for a discrete-time linear system affected by uncertainty in a computationally tractable way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast to the traditional approach to robust optimization, our approach is computationally tractable and, moreover, it can be applied to infinite-horizon optimization of uncertain discrete-time linear systems.
, in a wide variety of control synthesis problems, a judicious choice of the parameterization of the control law may render the control problem computationally tractable.

, with the new parameterizations, the control law synthesis problem is reduced to solving a sequence of convex programs, which is a significant computational improvement over the traditional approach.
